transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-01-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Jenna Morales (Northwind Head of ML), Tom Reyes (SRE), Ishaan Kapoor (Product), Lily Zhang (QA)

Summary:
Quick POC weekly check-in focusing on model quality drift observed in last run, guardrail false positives, and scoring adjustments. Decide to run targeted reruns with KV cache and alternate quantization, scope canary for dedicated capacity, and collect 3 edge prompts from customer.

Topics covered:
- Recent regression: hallucination in invoice parsing examples
- Scorecard threshold bumping vs. per-prompt weights
- Guardrail false positives for vendor names
- KV-cache and batching impact on latency/cost
- Dedicated vs hosted for stability and SLA

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Ok, hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we wanted to run through the latest stability heatmap and the two regressions you flagged last week. Jenna, do you wanna start with a quick recap of the failures you saw?
[00:18] Jenna Morales: Yeah thanks Maya. So we had about 1.8% of the invoice parsing set suddenly jump in hallucination class, specifically currency fields being swapped, um and a couple vendor names turned into weird tokens, like "Nort's Wind" instead of Northwind, uhm so it's small but it affects our downstream reconciliation.
[00:36] Raj Patel: When you say swapped currency fields, is that on long sequences or short ones? I ask because batching/kv cache changes behavior across seq length.
[00:49] Jenna Morales: Mostly mid-length, around 250 to 450 tokens. We think it's edge context mixing from previous prompts in the batch.
[01:06] Tom Reyes: Also callout from infra — latency spiked in the 2 PM ET window, we saw GPU stalls, not sure if it's on your side or our orchestration.
[01:18] Maya Chen: Right, we're looking at the telemetry. Raj, we pushed a run with kv-cache disabled last night, the preliminary shows lower stalls but slightly higher token cost.
[01:34] Raj Patel: Mm-hmm, the tradeoff is classic — KV caching reduces compute for repeated prefixes but if it's misaligned with your request distribution, it can cause cross-contamination if batching isn't session-aware. We suspect the batch boundaries were too wide.
[01:49] Isabella— sorry, I mean Lily?
[01:53] Lily Zhang: Yeah sorry. We've also seen a few false positives from your guardrail when vendor names include punctuation — the regex-based guard rejects correct entries, it's causing a bunch of manual triage.
[02:06] Maya Chen: Ok that's important. Are those guardrails coming from our standard name-list rules, or custom rules you added?
[02:12] Lily Zhang: Mostly standard, but our invoices have lots of DSL like "N-W Logistics, LLC" with hyphens and parens.
[02:20] Raj Patel: We can switch to the fuzzy name matcher in the guardrail layer — it'll reduce false positives but may slightly increase permissiveness.
[02:31] Jenna Morales: We're worried about permissiveness, because compliance requires that vendor name mismatches be less than 0.2% for audit.
[02:42] Maya Chen: Understood, so the action will be to create a whitelist++ approach — fuzzy match but with stricter score floor for high-value vendors. We'll note that.
[02:51] Tom Reyes: On the infra side, if you folks are recommending dedicated pools for stability, we need to understand the egress and firewall implications. We can't have unpredictable public IP ranges.
[03:03] Raj Patel: For Dedicated we can provide fixed egress IPs and a VPC peering plan, though in the private on-prem option we can do wholly customer-hosted. We should map that to your security checklist.
[03:18] Maya Chen: I'll attach our VPC network diagram and egress IP list to the follow-up.
[03:23] Ishaan Kapoor: Quick question on scoring — right now the scorecard treats hallucination and formatting errors equally. Can we scope per-error-type weights so that currency hallucination gets higher penalty?
[03:35] Raj Patel: Yes, the scorecard supports per-assertion weights. We can bump the hallucination penalty and then re-run the threshold scan to optimize precision/recall.
[03:46] Jenna Morales: That sounds good. Also, can you run the rerun with quant-8 and quant-4 variants? We want to see if quantization introduced any regressions.
[03:57] Raj Patel: We'll run the same sample across float16, q8_0 and q4_0 quant profiles. Quick note — q4 may change tokenization edge-cases, so expect a small delta.
[04:08] Maya Chen: Great. For timeline, Raj, can you do the KV-cache enabled vs disabled comparison plus quant experiments and share a short table?
[04:16] Raj Patel: Yes, I can. I'll run 2k samples representative of your distribution and output: per-prompt score, latencies p50/p95, token counts, and cost estimate.
[04:27] Lily Zhang: If you're running on dedicated, do we need to book instances in advance for the rerun?
[04:33] Raj Patel: We'll use hosted for these diagnostics to be faster. If you want the same environment as production, we can schedule a dedicated dry-run once we have the config.
[04:45] Maya Chen: Ok we'll set up a canary for 1 hour on dedicated once we agree on config.
[04:51] Jenna Morales: Another oddity — some prompts that reference vendor abbreviations like NWL-123 are getting mapped to other entities by the NER. Could that be a tokenization collision?
[05:03] Raj Patel: Possibly. Token collisions can happen with short dashed tokens. We can add a normalization pre-step to the pipeline to protect abbreviations, then mark them as non-candidate for NER alteration.
[05:16] Ishaan Kapoor: On acceptance criteria — our PM wants automated rollback if the daily error rate exceeds 0.5% after rollout. Can Redwood OE a rollback hook?
[05:28] Maya Chen: We have a rollback policy: canary + automatic rollback if a metric breaches threshold. We'll set up the metric-alert and automated flip to previous model variant.
[05:38] Tom Reyes: What about auditing? We need immutable logs for each inference and store of prompts for 90 days for compliance.
[05:48] Lena Ortiz: We have configurable retention windows and can push logs to your S3 with server-side encryption and KMS-managed keys. We'll verify retention and access logs.
[05:59] Jenna Morales: Are there any known issues with KMS integration and dedicated?
[06:05] Raj Patel: No major issues, customers use KMS all the time. We'll need key ARNs and some setup in your account for the VPC/private deployment.
[06:15] Maya Chen: Ok, I'm gonna put a concrete checklist in the follow-up: KMS ARNs, egress IPs, 3 edge prompts, run results.
[06:22] Lily Zhang: For the edge prompts — do you prefer them as raw invoices or json with fields?
[06:28] Jenna Morales: JSON with fields please, that helps with scoring.
[06:33] Raj Patel: Noted.
[06:35] --- brief silence / background typing ---
[07:10] Raj Patel: Going back to the guardrail false positives — do you have a sample of the tripped items? If you can share 50 examples we can tune thresholds without impacting production.
[07:22] Lily Zhang: I'll pull 50 and also mark which ones were manually corrected.
[07:27] Maya Chen: That will be super helpful. Also, please flag high-value vendors for stricter matching.
[07:34] Jenna Morales: One more thing — we saw the model hallucinate a line item price that wasn't in the invoice, and that cascades to reconciliation. How do you suggest we guard price fields?
[07:46] Raj Patel: Best approach is deterministic extraction for price fields — use a secondary rule-based extractor plus model verification. If the model disagrees with rules, mark for review. That hybrid approach reduces hallucination.
[07:59] Ishaan Kapoor: Can we configure the system so that price fields require 95% model+rule agreement to pass?
[08:08] Raj Patel: Yes, we can set a composite pass threshold. We'll add that to the scorecard config.
[08:16] Maya Chen: Ok. Quick pause — let me recap the technical runbook we agreed: 1) Run 2k-sample across float16/q8/q4 with KV-cache toggled; 2) Produce per-prompt scores + latency/cost table; 3) Tune guardrail fuzzy matcher + whitelist for high-value vendors; 4) Collect 50 tripped guardrail examples and 3 edge-case prompts from Northwind; 5) Schedule a dedicated canary dry-run. Any additions?
[08:41] Jenna Morales: Add the KMS/egress checklist for security sign-off.
[08:46] Maya Chen: Noted.
[08:49] Tom Reyes: One operational question — in case of a rollback, what's the exact time to flip? We need an SLA on rollback latency.
[08:59] Raj Patel: Rollback is immediate from control plane; propagation to all nodes depends on cache TTL but typically under 30s for serving routing.
[09:10] Tom Reyes: That's acceptable.
[09:13] Lily Zhang: Curious, has Redwood seen quant-4 leading to any silent hallucination spikes historically?
[09:23] Raj Patel: There's anecdotal cases; q4 compresses weights heavily so some subtle behaviors change. That's why we're running the cross-quant sweep.
[09:33] Jenna Morales: Ok. If the q4 delta is large, we'd probably stick to float16 in production.
[09:40] Raj Patel: Understood.
[09:43] --- brief cross-talk / background noise ---
[10:10] Maya Chen: I have one ask for the team — can we include a per-route breakdown in the report? This helps you map which prompt families cause the regressions.
[10:21] Raj Patel: Yes, we'll tag outputs by prompt family and include traffic buckets.
[10:27] Ishaan Kapoor: For the canary, what traffic % do you recommend?
[10:33] Raj Patel: Start at 2% for 1 hour, monitor the error metric and if stable open to 10% over next day.
[10:41] Jenna Morales: Sounds safe.
[10:44] Maya Chen: Great. Any blockers on timelines?
[10:48] Tom Reyes: We'll need to run the security review for dedicated — probably a 5-day SLA from our side.
[10:55] Maya Chen: Ok, we'll factor that into scheduling.
[10:58] --- pause, typing ---
[11:35] Raj Patel: One more note — in your prompt preprocessing you have trailing whitespace and newline variations that change tokenization; normalizing whitespace will reduce variance.
[11:47] Lily Zhang: Good call, we'll normalise.
[11:52] Jenna Morales: I'll coordinate with QA to provide the prompt set and acceptance criteria by Monday.
[11:57] Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll send a follow-up with the runbook and pricing.
[12:05] --- Meeting wrap-up ---
[12:20] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps — Raj to run diagnostics (2k) and share table by 2026-01-26; Maya to send VPC and pricing by 2026-01-27; Ishaan to supply edge prompts by 2026-01-25; Tom to confirm firewall list by 2026-01-28; Lily to share 50 guardrail tripped examples by 2026-01-24.
[12:45] Jenna Morales: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
[12:50] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
